Where to Stay in Suphan Buri?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Suphan Buri hotels across every budget — from a top-scoring budget hotel in the town centre and a 4-star with pools to a lakeside in-town stay, treehouses by Bueng Chawak and resorts in Sam Chuk and U Thong. Covering the town centre, Bueng Chawak, Sam Chuk and U Thong. From roughly ฿590–1,300/night.
introH2: 🏯 Why does choosing the right area in Suphan Buri matter so much?
introHtml: Suphan Buri is an easy trip — about 90 minutes' drive from Bangkok — but its sights are spread across several districts, so where you stay really shapes the trip. Stays fall into four areas with different feels — the town centre has the Banharn–Jaemsai Tower, the Dragon Descendants Museum, markets and plenty of restaurants, best if you want to explore in town without driving far; Bueng Chawak (Doem Bang Nang Buat) is about 55 km from town, with an aquarium, a zoo and riverside stays, great for families staying near the lake; the Sam Chuk Hundred-Year Market is an old riverside market on the Tha Chin you can wander for half a day; and Don Chedi–U Thong to the south has the Don Chedi monument and the ancient town of U Thong. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth all day. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Suphan Buri hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Suphan Buri has no metro and no commercial airport — most people drive themselves or take a van/coach from Bangkok (Southern or Mo Chit terminals), about 90 minutes. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Rua Yai–Tha Phi Liang–Tha Rahat) is near Banharn Tower, the Dragon museum, markets and restaurants, best for exploring in town; Bueng Chawak (Doem Bang Nang Buat) is about 55 km out, ideal for an overnight by the aquarium and zoo; Sam Chuk is for the Hundred-Year Market on the Tha Chin River; and Don Chedi–U Thong to the south suits the monument and the ancient town. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Hop Inn Suphanburi
entries.revCount: 87 reviews · scores 9.2, the top in this guide
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Malaiman Rd · Rua Yai · town centre
tags: 🏨 Hop Inn chain · same standard everywhere
entries.addr: Malaiman Rd, Rua Yai, Mueang Suphan Buri
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Suphanburi is the budget hotel with the top guest score in this guide — 9.2 from 87 reviews. As part of the Hop Inn chain it delivers the same reliable formula everywhere — clean rooms, firm beds, cold air-con and free Wi-Fi. What guests like most is the generous car park and the Malaiman Road location near the Banharn–Jaemsai Tower. From just ฿700 there's no breakfast or fancy facilities, but if you want a clean, good-value room in town, this is the steadiest pick.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches a little, take a Standard with Balcony — you get a private balcony to sit out on for just a few baht more.

entries.name: Petchngam Home Resort
entries.badge: 🌿 High-scoring garden rooms near U Thong
entries.mrtTag: 📍 U Thong · near Don Chedi · outskirts
entries.storyHtml: Petchngam Home Resort is the second-highest scorer in this guide — 8.8 from 40 reviews, set in the U Thong area to the south. The rooms are air-con garden units of about 28 sqm with king beds, quiet and private, with parking right at the door. It's about 2 km from U Thong market and not far from the Don Chedi monument — a fit for anyone touring the south of the province who doesn't want to keep driving back into town. It sits roughly 25 km from the centre of Suphan Buri.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as three? Take the room that sleeps 3 — it splits cheaper per head — and check weekend prices ahead, as they rise above weekday rates.

entries.mrtTag: 📍 Prachathipatai Rd · Tha Phi Liang · town centre
entries.addr: Prachathipatai Rd, Tha Phi Liang, Mueang Suphan Buri
entries.storyHtml: Songphanburi Hotel is the only 4-star in this guide and the most facility-rich pick, scoring 8.2 from 149 reviews. Its draws are two swimming pools, a spa, a gym and breakfast, with a town-centre location on Prachathipatai Road within walking distance of the market and restaurants. It's a fit for families or anyone who wants a full-service hotel in town, from ฿900 — and the Family and Suite rooms comfortably fit a group.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family? Take the Family room — it's roomy with a separate sitting area and works out better than booking two standards.

entries.name: Country Lake View Hotel
entries.badge: 🌊 Lakeside in town · park at your door
entries.storyHtml: Country Lake View Hotel is the in-town lakeside hotel that gives you an airy waterfront feel without driving out of town, scoring 8.2 from 130 reviews. Its draw is the lakeside setting in the Tha Rahat area, with a riverside restaurant, parking at your door and even pet-friendly rooms for those bringing a dog along. The Deluxe rooms are around 40 sqm with large windows and breakfast — a fit for anyone who wants a waterside feel while staying close to town.

entries.storyHtml: Klindinaitawan Resort Samchuk is the boutique bungalow resort in the Sam Chuk area with a quiet, countryside feel near the Hundred-Year Market, scoring 8.2 from 64 reviews. The rooms are bungalow-style in a rural setting, breakfast is available, and it's a fit for anyone set on wandering the Sam Chuk Hundred-Year Market on the Tha Chin River who wants to stay close by rather than drive back into town. Room types run from singles up to family rooms for groups.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Visit the Sam Chuk Hundred-Year Market from morning to early afternoon when all the shops are open and it's cooler than midday — the resort is just a few minutes' drive away.

entries.storyHtml: Hotela Boutique Resort is the suburban boutique resort with rooms larger than the price suggests and plenty of reviews — 236, scoring 8.1. Rooms start at ฿690 for a Double, while the Deluxe and Suite are much bigger and suit groups or families. There's free parking and a pool table on site. It sits on a main road on the Rua Yai side, an easy drive into town — a fit for self-drivers who want a spacious room at a friendly price.

entries.storyHtml: Samchook Resort is the budget resort with the lowest starting price in this guide — from just ฿590, scoring 7.7. There are twin rooms in the main block and separate timber house/cottage units that feel more private, with breakfast on some rates and free parking. It's near Wat Sam Chuk and the Hundred-Year Market, a fit for budget travellers set on the old market who want to stay close by. Reviews are still few (4), so the data isn't as solid as the better-reviewed stays.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Suphan Buri hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Suphan Buri?
faq.a: It depends on your plans. The town centre (Rua Yai–Tha Phi Liang–Tha Rahat) is near Banharn Tower, the Dragon museum, markets and restaurants, best for exploring in town (Hop Inn, Lamoon, Songphanburi, Country Lake View, Vasidtee). Bueng Chawak (Doem Bang Nang Buat) is about 55 km out, ideal for an overnight by the aquarium and zoo (Bungchawak, The Sun). Sam Chuk is for the Hundred-Year Market on the Tha Chin River (Klindinaitawan, Samchook). U Thong to the south is near Don Chedi (Petchngam).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Suphan Buri hotels cost?
faq.a: Suphan Buri is affordable: budget stays start around ฿590–700 (Samchook, Hotela, Hop Inn, White House); 3-star hotels and boutiques are around ฿700–900 (Lamoon, Country Lake View, Klindinaitawan, Vasidtee, The Sun); and the 4-star and treehouse resorts start around ฿900–1,300 (Songphanburi, Bungchawak).

faq.q: ❓ Is it far to drive from Bangkok to Suphan Buri?
faq.a: Not far — it's about a 90-minute drive from Bangkok to central Suphan Buri (roughly 100–110 km), or you can take a van or coach from the Southern or Mo Chit terminals. Suphan Buri has no metro or commercial airport, so having a car is the easiest way to get around since the sights are spread across several districts. Almost every hotel has free parking.

faq.q: ❓ Which Suphan Buri hotels have a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide, the ones with a pool are Songphanburi Hotel (a 4★ in town with two pools, a spa and a gym) and The Sun Resort (bungalows with a pool near Bueng Chawak) — good for families who want the kids to swim.

faq.q: ❓ Want to visit Bueng Chawak — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you're set on the Bueng Chawak aquarium and zoo, stay on the Doem Bang Nang Buat side. The Sun Resort ฿800 is just about 160 metres from Bueng Chawak and has a pool. Bungchawak Resort ฿1,000 has treehouses and riverside row houses right by Bueng Chawak. Both are about 55 km from town, so a car helps.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Suphan Buri hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty. But on long weekends and holidays, small-room stays like Lamoon Boutique (9 rooms) and the resorts around Bueng Chawak fill fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more.
